newsitem.title: KENYA: Journalists' group denies failing in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Journalists' group denies failing in Rwanda.

text.p: A journalists' rights group denied on Friday that it acted improperly over a Rwandan newsreader accused of rape and taking a leading role in Rwanda's 1994 genocide.
Paris-based Reporters Sans Frontieres (RSF) denied accusations from the human rights group African Rights of a lack of research before it expressed concern about Joseph Ruyenzi at his arrest.
After his arrest last year, RSF expressed its deep concern and asked Rwanda's president to find out where he was being held and to secure his release if no charges were brought.

"Our position is first of all to ask for a fair trial and then we went there and made the proper research...We gave him some money because we thought before the trial that he was presumed innocent until proven guilty," an RSF spokesman said.

"We criticise African Rights for accusing us of not having done a proper job in Rwanda. We are astonished they accuse us of supporting Ruyenzi. We tried our best to obtain information on his case," he added.
Ruyenzi was charged with raping and sexually mutilating a woman during the genocide in 1994. He says he is innocent.

In a report issued on January 30, London-based African Rights said the handling of Ruyenzi's case by RSF and Amnesty International showed such agencies must closely investigate cases before publicising them to bring pressure on authorities.
African Rights says its eight-month investigation proves Ruyenzi is guilty and had a leading role in the genocide in which an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered.
Amnesty International said its actions were responsible in line with concern that due legal process should be followed.
